1999-01-07: Steve Jobs gave a keynote at MacWorld Expo, unveiling a family of see-through iMac-like G3 computers and a new line of multi-coloured iMacs.
1999-07-21: Steve Jobs launches Apple's new iBook laptop at MacWorld, with shares rising more than 2% to $55.
1999-08-31: Apple interim CEO Steve Jobs unveiled the G4 Power Macs at the Seybold publishing conference in San Francisco, claiming they would bring supercomputer power to the desktop.
1999-09-23: Steve Jobs, co-founder and interim CEO of Apple Computer, appeared tired and jetlagged at a Paris product launch where he introduced the new Apple Studio Display and G4 computer, after which he discussed Apple's market position and strategy.
2000-01-05: Steve Jobs announced he was dropping the "interim" title to become Apple's permanent chief executive.
2001-10-23: Steve Jobs unveiled the iPod to the world.
2002-01-24: Pixar Studios is selected by the Producers' Guild of America to receive its inaugural Vanguard Award, which may be given to Pixar executives possibly including Apple CEO Steve Jobs at a ceremony in Los Angeles on March 3.
2002-07-17: Apple CEO Steve Jobs is expected to give a keynote at MacWorld in New York.
2002-09-10: Steve Jobs gives the keynote at MacWorld in Paris, where Apple announces that iCal is available for download and that all new Macs will boot into Mac OS X by default from the start of next year.
2003-07-06: Steve Jobs is profiled as Apple Computer and Pixar Animations chief executive, with the past year's most dramatic development being the iPod personal music player and the launch of the iTunes music download service in the US.
2003-08-08: Pixar chief Steve Jobs threatens to take future films from Disney to another distributor unless new contracts are drawn up.
2004-01-06: Apple CEO Steve Jobs launched the iPod Mini, a cheaper and smaller version of the iPod music player, at the MacWorld show in San Francisco.
2004-01-08: Apple CEO Steve Jobs unveiled the iPod Mini at the MacExpo show, positioning it between the high-end iPods and cheaper flash-based music players.
2004-01-29: Pixar chief executive Steve Jobs said Pixar is ending talks to continue its relationship with The Walt Disney Co and will seek a deal with another studio.
2004-02-06: Pixar chief Steve Jobs attacked the Walt Disney Company over a lack of creative ambition, a week after announcing the companies would end their partnership by 2006.
2004-08-02: Apple CEO Steve Jobs was recovering from weekend surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his pancreas, saying he would take August off to recuperate and expected to return in September.
2004-08-04: Steve Jobs announced he expects a full recovery from cancer surgery and plans to return to work next month, raising succession questions at Apple and Pixar.

A USA Today column criticizes Steve Jobs for Apple's control-freak tendencies in the iPod era, comparing Apple to Singapore and saying he is repeating mistakes made with the Mac, while noting Jobs was not at Apple when the Mac OS licensing decision was made in 1985.
2005-01-16: A timeline notes that in 1976 Steve Jobs insisted he and Steve Wozniak try to sell the Apple I, leading to Apple Computer's founding in April 1976.
2005-02-10: Pixar chief Steve Jobs said his animation company would not renew its deal with Disney next year.
2005-04-28: Apple attempted to veto an unofficial biography of Steve Jobs and removed other books by the author from its stores.
2005-06-06: Steve Jobs announced at the Worldwide Developer Conference that Apple will transition its Macs from PowerPC to Intel processors, with Intel-based Macs shipping in 2006 and the transition completed by the end of 2007.
2005-07-18: Steve Jobs is described as co-founder and chief executive of Apple Computer and Pixar, with the iPod transforming Apple's fortunes and changing how music is consumed.
2005-09-07: Apple chief Steve Jobs unveiled the iPod nano, a flash-based music player replacing the iPod mini.
2005-09-08: Apple chief Steve Jobs unveiled the iPod nano, a flash-based music player replacing the iPod mini.
2006-01-10: Steve Jobs is expected to deliver the keynote at the annual Macworld conference in San Francisco, where he is anticipated to unveil new Apple products.
2006-01-20: Disney is reportedly in talks to acquire Pixar in an all-share deal that would make Steve Jobs Disney's biggest individual shareholder.
2006-01-24: Disney announces a $7.4bn all-share acquisition of Pixar, making Steve Jobs the largest single shareholder in Disney with an estimated 7% stake and a seat on the Disney board.
2006-01-27: Rumors suggest Disney may acquire Pixar, potentially making Steve Jobs Disney's largest shareholder and raising concerns at Microsoft about Apple gaining preference in digital distribution.
2006-02-28: Steve Jobs claimed that the new Intel-based Mac minis are respectively between 2.5-3x and 5.5x faster than their PowerPC ancestors and said Apple is on track to convert its entire line of Macs to Intel-based processors by the end of the year.
2006-09-12: Steve Jobs announced new iPods, iPod nanos, iTunes 7, movie downloads, and a planned “iTV” wireless streaming device at an Apple event.
2006-12-29: Apple's internal probe found that CEO Steve Jobs was aware of favorably backdated stock option grants but did not financially benefit from them, as the options were cancelled before being exercised.
2007-01-04: Steve Jobs is expected to give a keynote speech at the Macworld show in San Francisco next week to unveil new rumored products.
2007-01-09: Apple chief executive Steve Jobs confirmed the company is to launch the iPhone, a touchscreen handset combining mobile phone, internet access, and iPod music and video playback features.
Former Apple employee David Sobotta comments on Apple's announcements, including the iPhone, and says history may look more favorably on Bill Gates than Steve Jobs.
2007-01-10: Cisco Systems sues Apple over the iPhone name, a dispute that marred the launch despite Steve Jobs having hoped to secure an agreement before the high-profile launch.
2007-01-11: Apple CEO Steve Jobs presents the new iPhone.
2007-01-23: Steve Jobs was questioned by SEC investigators regarding backdated stock options.
2007-02-16: Cisco gives Steve Jobs' Apple until February 21 to respond to its lawsuit over the use of the name iPhone.
2007-04-25: Apple's board publicly declares "complete confidence" in Steve Jobs' integrity and leadership amid a stock options scandal, as former CFO Fred Anderson accuses Jobs of lying about his involvement.
2007-09-05: Steve Jobs introduced new iPods, including the iPod Touch, at an Apple event and announced a price cut for the 8 GB iPhone from $599 to $399.
2007-09-06: Steve Jobs issued an open letter apologizing to early iPhone buyers and announced a $100 store credit after Apple cut the iPhone price by $200.
2007-09-18: Apple CEO Steve Jobs confirmed that the iPhone will go on sale to British customers in November, with O2 as the sole UK operator.
2008-01-15: Steve Jobs is scheduled to deliver the keynote speech at MacWorld in San Francisco.
2008-06-09: Apple CEO Steve Jobs unveiled the new iPhone 3G, featuring GPS, faster 3G internet, and a lower price, at the Worldwide Developers Conference.
2008-07-14: Apple CEO Steve Jobs announced that the new iPhone 3G sold more than 1 million units in the three days since its launch, calling it "a stunning opening weekend."
2008-07-24: Steve Jobs called journalist Joe Nocera to dispute his reporting on Jobs's health, offering off-the-record details but refusing to share them with shareholders.
2008-08-28: Bloomberg briefly published a pre-written obituary for Steve Jobs before retracting it about 30 seconds later.
2008-08-29: Bloomberg accidentally published Steve Jobs's obituary prematurely and issued a retraction.
2008-09-09: Steve Jobs introduced Apple's iPod lineup updates and iTunes 8 at a launch event, his first major public appearance since June, and referenced rumors about his health by quoting Mark Twain.
2008-12-16: Apple announced that Steve Jobs would not give the keynote speech at Macworld and would no longer attend Macworld Expo events.
2008-12-17: Apple announced that Steve Jobs will not give the keynote address at the January Macworld show, the first time in 12 years, with Phil Schiller replacing him, raising questions about Jobs's health.
2008-12-18: Apple announces that CEO Steve Jobs will no longer give the keynote address at Macworld Expo, fueling concerns about his health.
2008-12-30: Gizmodo reports a rumor that Steve Jobs's health is declining rapidly, which CNBC's Jim Goldman disputes, saying Apple reiterated that Jobs's decision to skip the Macworld keynote was unrelated to his health.
2009-01-05: Steve Jobs revealed in an open letter that he has a hormone imbalance causing weight loss and will continue as Apple CEO while recovering.
2009-01-06: Steve Jobs did not appear at Apple's final Macworld keynote, where Phil Schiller instead gave the presentation.
2009-01-08: Steve Jobs did not appear at Apple's final Macworld keynote, where Phil Schiller delivered the presentation instead.
2009-01-14: Apple CEO Steve Jobs announced he is taking a medical leave of absence until the end of June, with Tim Cook responsible for day-to-day operations.
News reports state that Steve Jobs will be out until at least June due to health issues, prompting a dispute between journalist Dan Lyons and CNBC's Jim Goldman.
2009-01-15: Steve Jobs takes time away from Apple to deal with health problems, with Tim Cook serving as temporary replacement.
2009-01-16: Steve Jobs is reportedly considering a liver transplant to treat a consequence of the neuroendocrine cancer he was treated for in 2004, according to an unconfirmed Bloomberg report.
2009-01-21: Apple chief executive Steve Jobs is taking a six-month leave from the company due to "complex" health issues.
2009-01-23: Apple co-founder and CEO Steve Jobs was forced to take a leave of absence for health reasons.
2009-01-24: A Tech Weekly special reflects on the 25th anniversary of Apple unveiling the Macintosh, noting that Steve Jobs called some people "idiots."
2009-06-19: It was reported that Steve Jobs had a liver transplant two months earlier, which was disclosed late on Friday night.
2009-06-20: Steve Jobs underwent a liver transplant earlier in 2009, according to a Wall Street Journal report, though Apple refused to confirm or deny the claim.
2009-06-22: Apple CEO Steve Jobs is quoted in a press release announcing that over one million iPhone 3GS models were sold in the first three days after its worldwide launch.
2009-06-23: Methodist University Hospital in Memphis confirmed that Steve Jobs had received a liver transplant at its Transplant Institute.
2009-09-09: Steve Jobs said Apple does not see e-books as a big market and suggested general-purpose devices will win over dedicated e-book readers.
Steve Jobs appears on stage at an Apple event, receiving a standing ovation, and says he is back at Apple after a liver transplant.
2009-10-13: Steve Jobs is reportedly helping Walt Disney overhaul its retail stores into miniature theme parks by sharing Apple's retail techniques.
2010-06-07: Steve Jobs is due to unveil the fourth version of Apple's iPhone at the company's Worldwide Developer Conference in San Francisco.
2010-11-23: Apple's first computer, the Apple I, sold at auction in London for £133,250, together with its original packaging and a signed letter from Steve Jobs.
2011-01-17: Apple CEO Steve Jobs announced he is taking a medical leave of absence to focus on his health, while continuing as CEO and remaining involved in major strategic decisions, with Tim Cook responsible for day-to-day operations.
2011-02-23: Apple shareholders seeking to force the company to disclose a succession plan for ailing founder Steve Jobs, who is on medical leave with cancer, lost a vote on the issue at Apple's annual meeting in San Francisco.
2011-03-02: Steve Jobs made a surprise appearance at an Apple event to launch the updated iPad 2, despite being on indefinite medical leave.
2011-05-31: Steve Jobs is to take to the stage at Apple's Worldwide Developer Conference in San Francisco next week to launch iOS 5, Mac OS X Lion, and iCloud.
2011-08-24: Steve Jobs resigned as chief executive of Apple, to be replaced by Tim Cook, and was elected chairman of the board.
2011-08-25: Steve Jobs is described as having departed as Apple CEO, with Tim Cook identified as his successor.
Steve Jobs resigns as Apple chief executive, causing Apple shares to fall nearly 3% at the start of trading on Wall Street.
2011-08-27: Steve Jobs's resignation as Apple CEO was the most discussed in corporate history, prompting widespread speculation about Apple's future without him.
2011-10-04: Apple launched the iPhone 4S, its first iPhone launch after Steve Jobs retired and Tim Cook took over as CEO.
2011-10-05: Steve Jobs, co-founder and CEO of Apple, died after a long struggle with pancreatic cancer.
2011-10-06: Steve Jobs, the co-founder and former CEO of Apple, died, prompting an outpouring of sentiment and reflections on his legacy.
2011-10-10: Sony Pictures is set to acquire rights to Walter Isaacson's authorized biography of Steve Jobs for a planned biopic.
2011-10-14: The iPhone 4S, unveiled a day before Steve Jobs died, went on sale with thousands queuing outside Apple stores worldwide.
2011-10-16: Tim Berners-Lee praised Steve Jobs for insisting computers could be usable rather than infuriating, crediting the NeXT computer he used to write the World Wide Web software.
Steve Jobs' biographer Walter Isaacson reveals that Jobs regretted delaying surgery for pancreatic cancer in 2004 and instead pursuing alternative therapies.
2012-04-02: Ashton Kutcher is cast as Steve Jobs in one of two competing biopics about the late Apple founder.
2012-05-03: Magnolia Pictures acquires a previously lost 1995 Steve Jobs interview for US distribution, with a cinema release planned for the following week.
2012-10-05: A Guardian article marks the one-year anniversary of Steve Jobs's death by soliciting stories about the Apple co-founder's life.
2013-01-25: The biopic "jOBS," starring Ashton Kutcher as Steve Jobs, is due to receive its world premiere at the Sundance film festival.
2013-01-26: Steve Wozniak criticized the Steve Jobs biopic "jOBS" after a clip was released online, saying the portrayal of his relationship with Jobs was "not close" and the personalities were "very wrong."
2013-08-21: Ashton Kutcher and Steve Wozniak publicly disagree over Kutcher's portrayal of Steve Jobs in the biopic Jobs, with Wozniak criticizing the film and Kutcher questioning Wozniak's motives.
2014-07-08: Steve Wozniak says that most of the most creative people who worked on the Macintosh at Apple told him they would never, ever work for Steve Jobs again.
2014-10-15: Christian Bale is reported to be in line to play Steve Jobs in a forthcoming biopic after Leonardo DiCaprio backed out.
2014-10-31: Seth Rogen is in early talks to play Steve Wozniak in Danny Boyle's Steve Jobs biopic, with Christian Bale in line to play Steve Jobs.
2014-11-04: Christian Bale leaves the Steve Jobs biopic, becoming the second high-profile actor to pass on the role after Leonardo DiCaprio.
2015-07-03: Steve Wozniak commented on the trailer for Danny Boyle's Steve Jobs film, saying accuracy is second to entertainment and that he felt the real Jobs was present though exaggerated.
2015-09-04: The documentary "Steve Jobs: The Man in the Machine," a critique of the late Apple co-founder, is released in the US.
2015-09-17: Apple CEO Tim Cook criticizes recent Steve Jobs films as "opportunistic" during an interview on the Late Show with Stephen Colbert.
2015-10-03: Michael Fassbender, who plays Steve Jobs in Danny Boyle's biopic, joked at the New York Film Festival that he studied Ashton Kutcher to prepare for the role.
2015-10-09: Former Apple CEO John Sculley says Steve Jobs would have mostly liked the new biopic "Steve Jobs" but would have been hurt that viewers might think they know the complete Steve Jobs.
2015-11-23: Pixar president Ed Catmull says Steve Jobs would have been "appalled" by Danny Boyle's biopic, claiming it fails to accurately represent him.
2016-07-05: Apple announces that its upcoming iOS 10 update will let US iPhone users sign up as organ donors, a move CEO Tim Cook linked to Steve Jobs' 2009 wait for a liver transplant.
